subject: english-language

moments.title: Martha's Vineyard
moments.body: 1962: Labov's first major study examines the pronunciation of /aw/ and /ay/ on Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts. Local fishermen are showing exaggerated traditional pronunciation as a way of maintaining identity against summer tourists. Linguistic change tracks social identity.
moments.takeaway: The Martha's Vineyard study is one of the founding texts of variationist sociolinguistics.

moments.title: NYC department store survey
moments.body: Labov's PhD research (1962-64, published 1966) on r-pronunciation in NYC. He asks shop assistants in Saks (high-end), Macy's (mid), and S. Klein (working-class) for the location of items 'on the fourth floor'. Repeated to elicit careful and casual styles. The pattern: more /r/ pronunciation in higher-class stores; assistants shift in careful speech.
moments.takeaway: The /r/ variable was a class marker; everyone knew it (the rapid style shift showed this). The result was a foundational finding of modern sociolinguistics.

moments.title: Sociolinguistic methodology
moments.body: Labov's 'Sociolinguistic Patterns' (1972) defined the methodology. Variation by class, gender, age, ethnicity, style is now the framework for sociolinguistic study. Peter Trudgill (Norwich 1974), Penelope Eckert (Detroit high schools, 1989), Peter Patrick and others extended the approach.
moments.takeaway: Labov is one of the most-cited modern linguists. His combination of rigorous quantitative method with social interpretation defined the field.

now.title: Variationist sociolinguistics today
now.body: Modern sociolinguistics has expanded to include ethnographic methods, identity, indexicality (Penelope Eckert's third wave). Studies of MLE, AAE (African American English), regional variation continue. Computational sociolinguistics uses Twitter and other corpora.
now.open_questions: How do social factors and language interact? Modern sociolinguistics has developed nuanced theories — class, gender, race, identity, network — but the core insight (linguistic variation is socially structured) remains Labovian.

reflection: One study in Manhattan department stores founded a field. Labov's combination of method, quantitative analysis and social interpretation showed how social structure shows up in everyday speech — and gave linguists tools to study the relationship.
